findings.title: Workspace reads can disclose secrets without confirmation
findings.rationale: Direct reads and directory discovery classify paths under the D-01 catalog before protected names or bytes are exposed; sensitive/absolute-deny entries fail closed and listings report only an aggregate omitted count.
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for unprotected automatic sensitive reads; discovery ignore rules and one-run exceptions remain later e06 stories.
findings.residual_risk: Users must renew authority for sensitive session resume; absolute-deny remains non-overridable.

findings.title: Streaming drops provider-required assistant fields
findings.rationale: Unknown streamed assistant extension fields are assembled and replayed across a tool round with offline regressions.
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for the historical field-loss defect.
findings.residual_risk: Provider-specific streamed shapes require maintained synthetic fixtures and are not a live release gate.

findings.title: Stdout is not final-answer-only
findings.rationale: Normal, verbose, streaming, and tool-round regressions keep final answers on stdout and operational output on stderr.
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for the historical stdout contamination defect.
findings.residual_risk: Candidate wheel behavior still requires final release verification.

findings.title: Expected CLI failures escape as tracebacks
findings.rationale: cli.main translates expected connection, session, credential, provider, and validation failures into one secret-free stderr diagnostic with nonzero exit and no traceback; final-answer stdout stays empty on those failures.
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for expected CLI traceback leakage.
findings.residual_risk: Unexpected programming defects can still raise; only expected operational failures are translated at the CLI boundary.

findings.title: Metadata-only and Codex operations unnecessarily require keyring
findings.rationale: Credential-store construction is lazy and metadata-only and Codex routes are regression-tested without keyring initialization.
findings.release_effect: The historical eager-keyring defect no longer blocks release.
findings.residual_risk: Native backend behavior may receive optional side testing but is not a release gate.

findings.title: Failed Codex login leaves a selected connection
findings.rationale: Delegated login now completes before metadata mutation and failed-login rollback is regression-tested.
findings.release_effect: The historical failed-login mutation no longer blocks release.
findings.residual_risk: Delegated CLI lifecycle requires maintained fake-executable regressions after e07 semantics are complete.

findings.title: The reviewed implementation has no reproducible release baseline
findings.rationale: The selected stabilization identity is 0.6.0 across pyproject metadata, orbitrelay.__version__, both CLI entry points, and isolated-wheel command output.
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for missing post-0.5.0 identity; tagging and publication still require later release-owner approval.
findings.residual_risk: Untagged source can still change after identity selection; e10 remains the candidate closeout.

findings.title: The official quality gate passes while quality gates fail
findings.rationale: scripts/check.sh now fails closed on Ruff, mypy, branch coverage (fail-under 80), pip-audit, and Bandit via scripts/run_quality_policy.py (e09s01/e09s02). A passing unit suite alone cannot bypass these stages.
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for missing terminal quality gates.
findings.residual_risk: Quality thresholds remain policy-bound and must be re-run on each candidate revision.

findings.title: Tool failures are reported as successful events
findings.rationale: Tool outcomes emit truthful statuses (ok/error/denied). Denied calls never enter an executing phase; process/tool failures are classified without treating denials as success (e08s06).
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for false-successful tool events.
findings.residual_risk: Future tools must continue to return Error:/structured error shapes recognized by observers.

findings.title: Corrupt sessions disappear and survive delete-all
findings.rationale: Corrupt sessions remain visible in list/show with secret-free diagnostics; inactive corrupt sessions are deletable; delete-all reports partial failures with nonzero exit (e08s03).
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for invisible corrupt sessions.
findings.residual_risk: Inaccessible/symlink session paths still fail closed and may need manual FS repair.

findings.title: Session persistence is not safe for concurrent processes
findings.rationale: SessionStore acquires a kernel-backed exclusive lease before history load and holds it through the run; concurrent owners fail or boundedly wait, and crash releases the lock. List/show report secret-free active status.
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for missing exclusive session ownership.
findings.residual_risk: Replay-safe checkpoints and corrupt-session lifecycle remain e08s02/e08s03.

findings.title: Session history is unbounded and rewritten repeatedly
findings.rationale: Session history uses pair-preserving durable segments with bounded resume memory; system instructions are current-on-resume; future history formats fail closed (e08s04).
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for unbounded session rewrite/load.
findings.residual_risk: Operators must keep segment/replay bounds aligned with provider context limits.

findings.title: Subprocess output capture is unbounded
findings.rationale: Python tool and Codex capture share deadlock-safe bounded drains with explicit timeout/truncation metadata; discarded content is never retained (e08s05).
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for unbounded subprocess capture.
findings.residual_risk: Bound constants are policy; extreme hosts may still need operator limits outside OrbitRelay.

findings.title: File writes are non-atomic and have a path race
findings.rationale: Workspace writes commit via temp+os.replace with validation-to-use rechecks; interruption before replace preserves prior target bytes (e08s06).
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for non-atomic workspace writes.
findings.residual_risk: Cross-filesystem renames are not supported; workspace must remain one filesystem.

findings.title: Import validation examines unrelated environment values
findings.rationale: Environment credential import was removed and the obsolete command is regression-tested as unsupported.
findings.release_effect: The superseded environment-import defect does not block release.
findings.residual_risk: None for the removed environment-import route.

findings.title: Denied tools emit an executing phase
findings.rationale: Approval records only emit executing for allowed dispositions; denied/disabled calls surface status=denied without an executing phase (e08s06).
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for denied-as-executing audit confusion.
findings.residual_risk: External consumers must prefer TOOL_RESULT status over phase heuristics.

findings.title: Context budgeting is not provider- or token-aware
findings.rationale: The current character budget is explicit and preserves tool pairs; provider-specific token accounting is deferred while e08s04 first establishes conservative bounded replay and overhead rules.
findings.release_effect: Non-blocking only if e08s04 proves a conservative compatibility bound for the stabilization candidate.
findings.residual_risk: Some provider or model limits can still be exceeded despite the character bound.

findings.title: Provider status reports metadata, not readiness
findings.rationale: provider status reports independent offline facts (configured, selected, catalog/model, credential present/absent/unavailable) and derives only local-ready, not-ready, or unknown without network access or secret values.
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for API-provider offline readiness vocabulary.
findings.residual_risk: Explicit live verification remains e07s02; readiness is offline/local only.

findings.title: Python 3.14-only packaging narrows adoption without proven need
findings.rationale: The approved target is Python 3.12 through 3.14, but metadata must remain at 3.14 until the complete macOS matrix supplies evidence.
findings.release_effect: The metadata change is deferred to e09s03 and remains a candidate gate rather than authority for an early edit.
findings.residual_risk: Users on Python 3.12 and 3.13 cannot install the package until qualification completes.

findings.title: Four Ruff findings remain
findings.rationale: The exact historical F401 and F841 categories pass an offline focused Ruff run.
findings.release_effect: The four July hygiene findings no longer block release; terminal lint policy remains MAJ-08 and e09s01 work.
findings.residual_risk: No pinned full-project Ruff policy is enforced yet.

findings.title: Static typing is incomplete
findings.rationale: Pinned mypy is a terminal official-check stage over src/orbitrelay with postponed annotations enabled for 3.12+ imports (e09s01/e09s03).
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for missing terminal typing gate.
findings.residual_risk: Dynamic tool seams remain intentionally flexible; full disallow_untyped_defs is not required for 0.6.0.

findings.title: A removed command is still recommended
findings.rationale: Migration/provider guidance now recommends the provider command rather than the removed profile command.
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for unusable profile recovery guidance.
findings.residual_risk: Legacy docs outside the repo may still mention profile commands.

findings.title: The CLI has no version command
findings.rationale: orbitrelay --version and python -m orbitrelay --version report the selected 0.6.0 identity consistently with package metadata and orbitrelay.__version__.
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for missing CLI version identity.
findings.residual_risk: Operators must still distinguish untagged development builds from a published tag.

findings.title: Several modules exceed the local maintainability target
findings.rationale: Module size alone has no demonstrated failure; the approved scope rejects cosmetic splitting and permits refactoring only when a stabilization outcome proves the seam.
findings.release_effect: Accepted as non-blocking for this release, with targeted deepening allowed only inside approved stories.
findings.residual_risk: Large orchestration modules remain harder to reason about and can increase change risk.

findings.title: Event redaction naming overstates its guarantee
findings.rationale: EventCollector stores run-local structured events and redacts on serialization (to_dict). Release evidence and summaries consume redacted dictionaries only. Documented as serialization-time redaction rather than store-time mutation.
findings.release_effect: Accepted residual naming risk for 0.6.0; not a security bypass in supported sinks.
findings.residual_risk: Custom EventCollector sinks must call to_dict()/redaction before persistence.

findings.title: Several dependencies are behind current releases
findings.rationale: pip-audit is a terminal quality-policy stage and fails closed when advisory data is unavailable; editable local package is skipped (e09s02).
findings.release_effect: No independent release block remains for missing dependency advisory policy.
findings.residual_risk: Advisory freshness depends on cache/network at check time.

implications: Release-owner selected 0.6.0 for the standalone stabilization candidate and reserved 1.0.0 for a later milestone.
Package, module, CLI, and wheel identity report 0.6.0 after e05s02.
Python metadata remains at 3.14 until the complete macOS 3.12 through 3.14 matrix passes.
Selecting 0.6.0 does not authorize tagging, publishing, or push.
